name: Port of Echuca

facts.claim: Living monument to the 1870s, when Echuca was the third largest port in Australia outside Sydney and Melbourne
Paddlesteamers depart daily from the Echuca Wharf, which originally ran 332 m in the 1880s
Discovery Centre has audiovisual displays on the inland river system, a working Evans Brothers sawmill and a steam display; PS Adelaide (built 1866) is moored at the wharf
Daily guided walking tours run twice a day; filming location of TV series All the Rivers Run

name: Barmah National Park

facts.claim: Park on Yorta Yorta Country on the Murray floodplain, with walking trails through forest and along waterways and the Murray River
Oven mounds used for cooking by Traditional Owners can be seen along the Lakes Loop Track and Broken Creek Loop Track

name: Dharnya Centre

facts.claim: Cultural hub of the Yorta Yorta people, inside Barmah National Park on Sand Ridge Track
Three walking trails start from the centre, including the 1.2 km Yamyabuc Trail loop with 13 interpretive markers on Yorta Yorta knowledge
Kingfisher river cruises on the Murray with an Aboriginal cultural focus; guided Yamyabuc walks led by a Yorta Yorta Knowledge Holder run on select days

name: Kyabram Fauna Park

facts.claim: Zoos Victoria wildlife park at Kyabram in the Goulburn Valley
55 hectares of bushland and wetlands with more than 400 native animals including koalas, dingoes, kangaroos, wombats, emus and a meerkat exhibit
Daily keeper talks, animal encounters, walking trails and a water play park

name: Terrick Terrick National Park

facts.claim: Park with granite outcrops, woodlands and endangered grasslands, popular with birdwatchers
Short, steep Grade 3 walk from the picnic area to the summit of Mt Terrick Terrick, with views over the park and farmland
Contains Victoria's most significant stand of White Cypress Pines, near Bennetts Rock
